citations.narrative:
The facility is not sanitizing the water receptacles for rabbits as often as necessary. In multiple rabbit enclosures, the
water bowl and reservoir contain a green to greenish brown debris or film. When the APHIS official asked how often the
water receptacles are cleaned, the facility representative stated that they are cleaned approximately every 3-4 weeks.
Failure to sanitize water receptacles when dirty can lead to a build up of debris, reduced water quality, and increased risk
of illness in animals. All watering receptacles shall be sanitized when dirty: Provided, however, that such receptacles shall
be sanitized at least once every 2 weeks.
To be corrected by October 7, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
